'''Neil James Cherry''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM|size=85%}} (29 September 1946 – 24 May 2003) was a New Zealand [[environmental science|environmental scientist]].

==Biography==
===Early life and family===
Cherry was born in [[Christchurch]] on 29 September 1946.<ref name="HBTQ">{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |author-link1=Alister Taylor |author-link2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=96}}</ref> His parents were James Conrad Cherry and Mona Hartley, who had married in 1940.<ref name="Part 1"/> Cherry could trace his ancestry back to the ''[[Cressy (ship)|Cressy]]'', one of the [[First Four Ships]] that started the settlement of [[Canterbury, New Zealand|Canterbury]].<ref name="Part 1">{{cite web |last1=Hunt |first1=Dorothy |title=Neil Cherry ONZM – his life and work: Part 1 |url=http://www.nzine.co.nz/features/neilcherry_lifestory_part1.html |publisher=NZine |access-date=14 May 2017 |date=28 March 2003 |archive-date=18 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180218230437/http://www.nzine.co.nz/features/neilcherry_lifestory_part1.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Cherry was educated at [[Christchurch Technical College]], and went on to study physics at the [[University of Canterbury]], graduating [[Bachelor of Science|BSc(Hons)]] in 1969 and [[PhD]] in 1971.<ref name="HBTQ"/> His doctoral thesis, supervised by R.G.T. Bennett and G.J. Fraser, was titled ''A study of wind and waves''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Cherry |first=N.J. |year=1971 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=A study of winds and waves |publisher=UC Research Repository, University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/13505 |doi=10.26021/8139 |url=https://ir.canterbury.ac.nz/handle/10092/13505}}</ref>

In 1968, Cherry married Gae Denise Miller, and the couple went on to have two children.<ref name="HBTQ"/>

===Career===
{{Expand section|date=June 2019}}
Cherry specialised most recently in the effects of [[electromagnetic radiation]] on human health, following his earlier work in [[meteorology]] and [[wind energy]].

===Politics===
{{Expand section|date=June 2019}}
At the {{NZ election link|1987}} he stood for the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] in the Christchurch electorate of {{NZ electorate link|Fendalton}}. He boosted Labour's vote by 6.73%, but fell 311 votes short of defeating the incumbent MP [[Philip Burdon]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Norton |first=Clifford |title=New Zealand Parliamentary Election Results 1946–1987: Occasional Publications No 1, Department of Political Science |year=1988 |publisher=Victoria University of Wellington Press |location=[[Wellington]] |isbn=0-475-11200-8 |page=225 }}</ref> Ahead of the {{NZ election link|1990}} he put himself forward to replace former Prime Minister [[Geoffrey Palmer (New Zealand politician)|Geoffrey Palmer]] as the Labour candidate for {{NZ electorate link|Christchurch Central}}. He lost out on the Labour nomination to [[Lianne Dalziel]] but was, by his own estimation, the second preference and pledged to campaign for Dalziel.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Malthus |first1=Nigel |title=Cherry says he was 'runner-up' |work=[[The Press]] |date=20 September 1990 |page=7 }}</ref>

Cherry served as a Councillor on the [[Canterbury Regional Council (Environment Canterbury)]] from 1992.<ref name="HBTQ"/>

===Later life and death===
[[Image:Windflow's prototype windmill.jpg|thumb|160px|right|Windflow Technology's prototype windmill was named "Neil" to honour Cherry]]
Cherry was diagnosed with [[motor neurone disease]] in 2001, and became increasingly immobile until his death in 2003.<ref name="Herald obit">{{cite news |title=Obituary: Dr Neil Cherry |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/iobituaryi-dr-neil-cherry/XUJL2R3NVH2NHGYR2VYVQ5N4NI/ |access-date=8 November 2021 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=30 May 2003}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 1990, Cherry was awarded the [[New Zealand 1990 Commemoration Medal]].<ref name="HBTQ"/> In the [[2002 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2002 New Year Honours]], Cherry was appointed an [[New Zealand Order of Merit|Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to science, education and the community.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/new-year-honours-list-2002 |title=New Year honours list 2002 |date=31 December 2001 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=28 June 2019}}</ref>
